messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed direct C-H arylation of an imidazole to form 5-(2-fluorophenyl)-1-methyl-1H-imidazole-4-carbonitrile (Shields et al., Nature 2021, reaction 3); choose the base, ligand, solvent, concentration and temperature.

Variables and options:
base:
B1: Base option 1
B2: Base option 2
B3: Base option 3
B4: Base option 4

ligand:
L1: Ligand option 1
L2: Ligand option 2
L3: Ligand option 3
L4: Ligand option 4
L5: Ligand option 5
L6: Ligand option 6
L7: Ligand option 7
L8: Ligand option 8
L9: Ligand option 9
L10: Ligand option 10
L11: Ligand option 11
L12: Ligand option 12

solvent:
S1: Solvent option 1
S2: Solvent option 2
S3: Solvent option 3
S4: Solvent option 4

concentration:
C1: Concentration option 1
C2: Concentration option 2
C3: Concentration option 3

temperature:
T1: Temperature option 1
T2: Temperature option 2
T3: Temperature option 3

Experiments so far (best first):
B3 | L3 | S3 | C2 | T3 -> 84.2%
B1 | L3 | S3 | C3 | T3 -> 78.4%
B1 | L3 | S3 | C2 | T2 -> 68.5%
B1 | L3 | S3 | C2 | T3 -> 59.8%
B3 | L4 | S3 | C1 | T3 -> 49.1%
B1 | L4 | S3 | C2 | T3 -> 48.1%
B1 | L3 | S3 | C1 | T3 -> 31.5%
B2 | L5 | S3 | C1 | T3 -> 6.2%
B1 | L1 | S4 | C1 | T3 -> 0.0%
B2 | L7 | S2 | C1 | T1 -> 0.0%

Propose exactly 5 NEW experiments not listed above. Return JSON:
{"picks": [{"base": "<label>", "ligand": "<label>", "solvent": "<label>", "concentration": "<label>", "temperature": "<label>", "reason": "<one sentence>"}]}

picks.reason: This tests whether the higher concentration that helped with B1 further improves the strongest observed B3/L3/S3/T3 condition.
This checks the lower-concentration boundary while retaining the best-supported base, ligand, solvent, and temperature.
This isolates a temperature change from the current top condition to see whether the lower temperature benefit observed with B1 also applies to B3.
This probes an alternative solvent under the otherwise highest-yielding known combination.
This tests whether an untried base can match or exceed B3 while holding the best-supported remaining conditions fixed.
